response:
It’s completely understandable to feel hurt and excluded when friends cancel plans but then post about going out without you. That kind of inconsistency is painful, and your feelings of frustration are valid.

Before sending a group text, it might help to take a moment to cool down and then reach out to one or two people individually. A calmer conversation where you express how their actions made you feel — rather than labeling their behavior — is more likely to lead to understanding and positive change in the friendship. People often respond defensively to criticism, even when it’s deserved, so framing it around your experience ("I felt hurt when…") can open the door to honest dialogue. You deserve friendships where you feel valued and included, and having a direct, respectful conversation can help clarify whether these relationships can grow or whether it might be time to invest in connections that feel more mutual.
